papers.what_it_is: QCi case study running continuous-weight Nasdaq-100 portfolio optimization on Dirac-3 over 2003-2024 with comparison to the index and to LocalSolver.

assertions.value: The case study solves 255 monthly-rebalanced continuous portfolio optimization problems on Dirac-3 per test over a 21-year period, 2003-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
quotes: We tested its performance on a 21-year period, from January 1st, 2003, to March 31st, 2024.
each test over the 21 year period involved solving 255 optimization problems on Dirac-3.
assertions.certainty_reason: Setup stated plainly by the vendor; the page itself says 252 months in one table caption, a small internal inconsistency.

assertions.value: QCi reports that the Dirac-3 optimized portfolio beat Nasdaq-100 in 138 of 255 months (54.1%), with lower monthly return volatility; the page notes the hyperparameter study is limited.
quotes: the optimal portfolio has outperformed the index in 138 out of 255 months, that is a rate of 54.1%.
the optimal portfolio delivered a slightly higher return with a significantly lower risk.
assertions.certainty_reason: Backtest by the vendor, no significance test, and the page admits only stocks with full history were used.

assertions.value: On the same portfolio problems, QCi states that Dirac-3 and LocalSolver (Hexaly) solution energies are similar, with LocalSolver slightly lower for some solutions.
quotes: We ran the portfolio optimization test over the 21 year period using LocalSolver (Hexaly) Optimizer, a leading classical optimization technology.
the energies are similar, although LocalSolver yields a slightly lower energy for some of the solutions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Directly stated; no timing comparison is given and the page lists time-to-solution comparison as future work.

assertions.value: QCi states relaxation schedule 4 gave the best results, and schedule 3 gave similar results with a significantly improved runtime.
quotes: As expected, the highest relaxation schedule of 4 yields superior results; however, using a relaxation schedule of 3 yields similar results with a significantly improved runtime.
assertions.certainty_reason: Directly stated by the vendor, with tables of returns and runtimes.

response = solver.solve(model, num_samples= 60 , relaxation_schedule= 1 )

papers.what_it_is: QCi case study of risk-based drone trajectory selection with a time constraint as a QUBO on Dirac-1, with a scalability fit up to 10,364 variables.
papers.why_not: Page states Dirac-1 as the device; Dirac-3 appears only as future work. Assertions carry context platform:dirac-1.

assertions.value: On a time-constrained lowest-risk route (Winchester Medical Center case), QCi says Dirac-1 returned a trajectory that honored the time limit, visiting 6 major-risk nodes and one manageable node for a risk score of 49.
quotes: This trajectory visits 6 major risk nodes and one manageable risk node, giving a risk score of 49.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single worked case; no classical solver was run on the time-constrained model.

assertions.value: QCi reports one 10,364-variable instance run five times on Dirac-1 with an average 13,852 seconds per solve, and concludes from polynomial fits that time-to-solution scales better than cubic.
quotes: At 10,364 variables, this instance was run on Dirac-1 five times and returned the average of 13,852 seconds per solve.
Dirac-1 was able to solve this NP-complete problem within polynomial time, even at large scale- more than 10,000 variables.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical fit on a few points does not show polynomial scaling for an NP-complete problem, and no solution-quality figure is given at that size.
